\n| `POST .../eval-runs` | Create a run from a `suiteId` (rerun; `serverIds` optional — defaults to the suite's saved servers) or
`suiteName` + inline `tests` + `serverIds` (new suite). `environmentId` (requires `suiteId`) runs against one of the suite's attac
hed environments instead. Responds `202` + `runId` |\n| `PATCH .../eval-suites/{suiteId}` | Edit suite settings, including `enviro
nmentIds` — the project environments the suite runs against (non-empty array sets/replaces, `null` clears) |\n| `PATCH .../eval-su
ites/{suiteId}/schedule` | Enable/disable scheduled runs; `environmentId` pins which environment they launch |\n| `GET .../eval-ru
ns/{runId}` | Run status, result, and summary — poll until terminal. Carries `gateWaiver`: the audited override in force over this
run's gate, or `null` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate` | The stored suite quality-gate report for this run (`passed` / `fail
ed` / `non_gateable` / `not_configured`). `not_configured` is a 200 report, never a missing route. A deployment that predates the
evaluator answers `422 FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/decision-summary` | **Start here when a run did not
pass.** The canonical run decision contract: the verdict and where it came from, counts labelled with the population they count, t
he run's own verdict decision, and per-trial diagnostics with the user-value chain, the first failed stage, the failure category,
evidence scoped to that stage, and one next action (paginated) |\n| `POST .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | Override a **faili
ng** run's release gate until `expiresAt` (required, future, max 30 days out), with a `reason` (required, max 500 chars). Manage t
ier. Does NOT change the run's `result` — the run keeps its verdict and the waiver is reported alongside it. `409` when one is alr
eady in force, returning the existing waiver |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers` | The waiver in force over a run, or `n
ull`. Readable by anyone who can view the run |\n| `DELETE .../eval-runs/{runId}/gate-waivers/{waiverId}` | Revoke a waiver, putti
ng the gate back. Idempotent — a second call reports the original revocation rather than restamping it |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{ru
nId}/iterations` | Per-iteration results: tool calls, token usage, latency (paginated) |\n| `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}/iterations/
{iterationId}/trace` | Full trace: messages + expected-vs-actual analysis |\n| `GET .../eval-suites/{suiteId}/runs` | Recent runs
for a suite, newest first |\n\n**Eval result ingestion** (`/projects/{projectId}/eval-ingest/...`) — how `@mcpjam/sdk` saves resul
ts from eval runs executed outside the platform (local dev, CI). The `{projectId}` segment accepts the literal `default` for the k
ey org's Default project. Most users never call these directly — set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` and the [SDK reporter](https://docs.mcpjam.c

om/sdk/concepts/saving-results.md) does:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../eval-ingest/report` | One-shot: cr
eate a run from finished results and finalize it |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/start` | Chunked flow: create (or idempotently re
use) a run by `externalRunId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/runs/iterations` | Append an iteration batch to a started run |\n| `POST
.../eval-ingest/runs/finalize` | Finalize a chunked run (idempotent) |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts` | Store one artifact's
raw bytes (widget HTML too large to send inline) and return its `storageId` |\n| `POST .../eval-ingest/artifacts/upload-url` | Ret
ired. Answers `410 Gone` with `details.code: \"SDK_UPGRADE_REQUIRED\"`. `@mcpjam/sdk` 8.17.0 and later upload artifacts with `POST

.../eval-ingest/artifacts` instead |

**Agent** (`/projects/{projectId}/agent`) — a headless assistant turn for
building conve

rsational surfaces (the MCPJam Slack app is the first consumer):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../agent` | R
un ONE assistant turn over a `messages` history (`{role: \"user\"\\|\"assistant\", content}` items, max 50 messages × 8 KB each, 9
6 KB total). The model is pinned server-side and billed to the project. The turn can read project servers/suites/runs and **create
eval suites**; it can NOT start runs — kick those off yourself with `POST .../eval-runs`. Responds synchronously with `reply`, th
e `toolCalls` it made, `createdResources` (ids + app links), and token `usage`. Capped at 4 concurrent turns per organization and
\\~90 s wall clock. **Not idempotent — never blind-retry**: dedupe on your own trigger identity, and on an error response check `d
etails.createdResources` (and, after a lost response, list suites) before retrying, or you'll create duplicates |\n\n**Studies** (

`/projects/{projectId}/studies...`):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies` | List the project's published
studies: name, access mode, attached servers, share link |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}` | One study's full read: model, system
prompt, tool-approval policy, resolved servers, the environment it publishes, and its insights envelope. The last two need workspa

ce membership and are **absent** for a share-link visitor, never null |

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Swarms and User Testing are enabled p
er organization.** Everything in the\n> four sections below is behind that gate, enforced server-side. If it is not\n> on for your
organization, the reads generally return empty and every **write**\n> — creating a persona or goal, launching a run, publishing a

study,
> requesting insights — answers `403` with a message naming the feature, not a
> `404` and not a validation error.
>
>
Five operations are deliberately outside the gate, because every one of them\n> *reduces* exposure and spend: cancelling a goal r
un, unpublishing a\n> study, and archiving a persona, goal or swarm (each one's `DELETE`). An\n> organization that loses access ca

n still stop what is running and clean up
> what it authored.
>
> Ask us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) if you wan

t it turned on.

**Swarms — authoring** (`/projects/{projectId}/personas...`, `.../goals...`,
`.../swarms...`) — the definition
s a swarm run executes. A **persona** is a\nreusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a\n**swarm** is
an authoring container holding defaults for the goals made\nunder it. Nothing here starts anything — launching is\n`POST .../goal

s/{goalId}/runs`.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../per
sonas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |\n| `PATCH .../personas/{
personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe |\n| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a pe
rsona. **409** while goals still reference it |\n| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |\n| `POST .../goals` | Create a goa
l (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |\n| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |\n| `PA
TCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |\n| `D
ELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |\n| `GET .../swarms`
| List swarm containers |\n| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |\n| `GET .../swarms/{swarm
Id}` | One swarm |\n| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their ow

n values |
| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |

**Swarms — generation**
— drafts a model writes for you. Both routes return\ncandidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create
\nroutes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempotency-Key` — a call\nwith no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and of

fering one would imply the
drafts are stable across retries when they are not.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST
.../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |\n| `P

OST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
